chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeaths a share of his property and does not know what a share is.
He said: Is there among you nothing of what has reached you from Ja'far and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them both) regarding that?
Then I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, we have not heard our companions mention anything about this from your fathers (peace be upon them).
He said: A share is one of eight.
I said: May I be sacrificed for you, how did it become one of eight?
He said: Do you not read the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He?
I said: May I be sacrificed for you, I do read it, but I do not know where its place is.

He said: The saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'The charities are only for the poor, the needy, those who work upon (acquiring) them, those with affectionate hearts, the necks (of human beings in captivity to be liberated), those in debt, for the sake of Allah and for the stranded traveler.'
Then he counted eight with his hand. He said: And so did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) divide it into eight shares. A share is one of eight.

key_terms.سَهْم: Share, a portion or part, specifically defined here as one of eight

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'share' in Islamic inheritance and charity according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida clarifies that the term 'share' (sahm) in bequests refers to one of the eight specific categories of recipients outlined in Surah At-Tawbah, verse 60. He emphasizes that this division is not merely theoretical but was practically implemented by the Prophet Muhammad, thereby establishing a direct link between Quranic exegesis and Prophetic tradition (Sunnah) in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith serves to resolve ambiguity in legal terminology by grounding the definition of 'share' in explicit Quranic evidence.
